title: China AI Power Report Act

The law aims to increase transparency, monitor environmental impact, and promote more efficient and sustainable AI deployment within the country.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025

summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed set of laws that aim to regulate the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability while encouraging innovation by setting standards for how AI can be built, tested, and used.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill aims to establish a requirement that artificial intelligence systems be accompanied by a detailed functional bill of materials—a clear listing of all components, data, and algorithms that make up the AI product. It also includes additional provisions to address related regulatory or safety concerns, ensuring that AI deployments are transparent and accountable.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

It seeks to establish clear standards, training for educators, and safeguards to help students and teachers understand and responsibly use AI technologies.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets strict safety, privacy, and content guidelines for AI-powered toys aimed at children, ensuring they cannot pose physical or psychological risks. It requires manufacturers to meet these standards, report safety data, and gives regulators the authority to enforce compliance and remove non‑compliant products from the market.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives believes that anyone living near an AI data center, as well as the community as a whole, has the right to understand what’s happening at the site. It emphasizes that local people should have a say in how the data center is built and run, ensuring transparency and community control.
